proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall the expiring previously voted increase in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes within the County of Manistee, State of Michigan, currently 0.9827 mill ($0.9827 per $1,000 of taxable value), be renewed and levied for a period of four (4) years, 2027-2030, both inclusive, and shall an additional 0.0173 mill ($0.0173 per $1,000 of taxable value) be approved and levied to restore previous millage reductions under the “Headlee Amendment” since this millage was last approved, resulting in the levy of 1.00 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), subject to reduction as provided by law, on taxable property in the County?
The purpose of this levy is to provide funds to be used for operation and maintenance of the Manistee County Library. It is estimated that a levy of 1.00 mill would provide revenue of $1,649,837 in the first calendar year, of which $28,542 would result from the additional 0.0173 mill. The revenue from this millage levy will be disbursed to the Manistee County Library.
A portion of the millage may be subject to capture by and disbursed to one or more tax increment financing entities, including the City of Manistee Brownfield Redevelopment Authority, the County of Manistee Brownfield Redevelopment Authority, and the County of Manistee Land Bank Authority.
proposals.officialTitle: LIBRARY MILLAGE RENEWAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 0.9827 mills for 4 years — generally no increase over what you pay now, plus the restored or added amount described.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall the Township of Bear Lake, County of Manistee, Michigan, borrow the principal sum of not to exceed Four Million Sixty-Five Thousand Dollars ($4,065,000), and issue its unlimited tax general obligation bonds payable in not to exceed twenty (20) years from the date of issue, to pay all or part of the cost of acquiring, constructing, furnishing and equipping a new fire station, including all site improvements, appurtenances and attachments?
If approved, the estimated millage to be levied in 2027 is 1.9532 mills ($1.95 per $1,000 of taxable value) and the estimated average annual millage rate required to retire the bonds is 1.9463 mills ($1.95 per $1,000 of taxable value).
proposals.officialTitle: Fire Station Bond Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $4.07 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.
